confirmed.fact: Enemy hit runs transform scale(.75 to 1.15) and opacity 1 to 0 over .6s; player hit runs opacity .45 to 0 over .5s. Both -webkit and standard keyframes remain active.
Effect wrapper is absolute, clipped and pointer-events:none, z-index:5. This separates DOM/stacking but does not remove animated properties or prove independent QtWebKit repaint.

The existing body background still contains the old entire battle UI frame including the central lower skull. Broad old frames could be from this artwork; this is a fingerprint to compare, not proven causality.
Global body pseudos draw fixed outer 8px left/bottom metal strips at z900. Profile stylesheet globally changes body:before y/height. They cannot by themselves draw the broad central skull frame.

Earlier actual non-profile CSSOM confirmed the profile body:before rule loads globally. Current renderers do not explicitly hide these pseudos; latest computed pseudo state during a visible symptom remains to be captured.

Earlier samples had body/html rect(0,0,1280,800), battle root rect(1,1,1280,800), unchanged during FX. This 1px inherited native origin is preexisting and does not explain a transient effect by itself. Latest final CSS uses newer fonts; do not call those old metrics current visual proof.
Current JS only normalizes redundant BRs. It does not animate, change styles, modify frames or recalculate game state.
SVG has static paths and gradient stops; no script, CSS animation, SMIL or external resource.

hypotheses.text: Animated transform/opacity changes WebKit layer composition or invalidation while old body artwork/outer pseudos participate in repaint. Disappearance at animation end is consistent with this but not sufficient proof.
The inherited 1px native origin exposes edges or amplifies raster rounding during repaint. Static DOM rectangles alone cannot distinguish paint artifacts.

steps: Keep the existing wrapper, all QSP output conditions and all geometry. Set both FX animations/transforms to none, slash opacity to1 and player flash opacity to1 with equivalent RGBA background.

Reuse the existing battle JS script loaded by both renderers. Hide only the existing effect nodes once with visibility:hidden after their .6/.5 second lifetime. No opacity/transform stepping, CSS transitions, intervals, persistent state, QSP changes or new assets.

Capture effect-off, CSS-animated baseline and static timed candidate at matching 25/120/350/650ms and during rapid repeated turns. Compare pixels outside the effect rectangles and report actual observed transient frames separately from DOM invariants.

Only as separate diagnosis, test hiding body pseudos or replacing body background with a solid reference color; do not combine these with the animation A/B or adopt a global border removal without scope review.
preserves: all combat calculations and output triggers
limits: Visibility toggling still repaints; it avoids the particular CSS animation path but is not a promise of no compositor or OS issues.
Using JS opacity/transform animation or promoting the root with translateZ/will-change would not cleanly isolate the suspected route.
Static slash loses growth/fade interpolation; image and visible lifetime can stay the same. Static player flash can be more visually abrupt.
Animated GIF/sprite assets introduce frame decoding/asset changes and are not the smallest controlled test.

runtimeNeeded: Exact screenshot pixels during live effect, not only after .6s
Root/body/native viewport rect and scroll metrics at those same times
Confirm slash and flash cause symptom independently or only together
Observe clicks and next-turn redraw after timer hides a detached old node

references.scope: QtWebKit reference: AcceleratedCompositingEnabled describes caching/composition of transform/opacity CSS animations when used with QGraphicsWebView. Actual installed rendering mode/flag is not established here.
Historical Qt WebKit bug describes platform-dependent opacity compositing and software transparency layers. This is mechanism evidence, not proof of this game defect.
WebKit documentation describes composition/clip handling during transform or opacity animations. No version/binary equivalence asserted.
